findings.reason: Untrusted source: balloon_onchannelcallback() (drivers/hv/hv_balloon.c:1488-1545) receives the Hyper-V host's DM_UNBALLOON_REQUEST into the static __u8 recv_buffer[PAGE_SIZE] (line 506) via vmbus_recvpacket(dev->channel, recv_buffer, PAGE_SIZE, &recvlen, &requestid) (lines 1491-1493); hv_ringbuffer_read() (drivers/hv/ring_buffer.c) sets *buffer_actual_len = packetlen from the host-written ring descriptor and only guards packetlen > buflen (i.e. <= PAGE_SIZE), so the message content including req->range_count is entirely host/peer-controlled. Missing local limit check (asymmetric validation): the dispatch at case DM_UNBALLOON_REQUEST (lines 1519-1523) calls balloon_down() with the only gate being recvlen > 0 (line 1495) - no hdr.size == sizeof(struct) check, no cross-check of range_count against recvlen/PAGE_SIZE, and no comparison against the guest's own ballooned-page bookkeeping - while the sibling message type of the same protocol, DM_MEM_HOT_ADD_REQUEST (line 1530 'if (ha_msg->hdr.size == sizeof(struct dm_hot_add))'), does validate the host header size: the mirror path of the same vmbus dynamic-memory protocol enforces a limit that the unballoon path does not. Unsafe use: balloon_down() (lines 1353-1363) fetches 'int range_count = req->range_count;' (line 1357) - a raw peer __u32 - and iterates 'for (i = 0; i < range_count; i++) free_balloon_pages(dm, &range_array[i]);' (lines 1362-1363) with no bound: range_count up to 2^31-1 walks range_array[] far past the PAGE_SIZE recv_buffer (OOB read of .bss/static memory), and each fetched union dm_mem_page_range then drives free_balloon_pages() (lines 1193-1206): 'int num_pages = range_array->finfo.page_cnt; __u64 start_frame = range_array->finfo.start_page;' (lines 1196-1197) -> 'pg = pfn_to_page(i + start_frame); __free_page(pg); dm->num_pages_ballooned--; ' (lines 1202-1204) - freeing host-chosen PFNs with no pfn_valid() check and underflowing num_pages_ballooned. This is the peer-trusted-transport invariant: peer-supplied count/length fields cross the guest-host channel into kernel iteration/allocation without cross-check against locally-known limits, exactly the seed's mechanism on a guest-host virtual bus. Counterevidence checked: hv_ringbuffer_read bounds the delivered recvlen to PAGE_SIZE (so the OOB is driven by range_count, not a short/long receive); alloc_balloon_pages()'s own error unwind (lines 1341-1345) frees only ranges the guest itself built; the DM_BALLOON_REQUEST path's num_pages is bounded by the PAGE_SIZE bl_resp->hdr.size accumulation check (line 1223) and alloc_pages failure. Attacker model is the hypervisor/host peer (semi-trusted in the drivers/hv threat model), which bounds real-world exploitability; no runtime reproducer was built (read-only snapshot, requires a Hyper-V host injecting a crafted DM_UNBALLOON_REQUEST).

Untrusted source: qcom_glink_rx_data() (drivers/rpmsg/qcom_glink_native.c:762-875) peeks the glink TX_DATA header out of the shared-memory RX fifo of the Qualcomm glink transport to the remote subsystem (modem/SSR peer) - a kernel-side client of a remote virtual device transport. The peer fields hdr.chunk_size and hdr.left_size (raw __le32 written by the remote peer, lines 787-788) are the only sizing inputs. Missing local limit check: the sole validation at line 790 'if (avail < sizeof(hdr) + chunk_size)' compares the peer field against glink_smem_rx_avail() (drivers/rpmsg/qcom_glink_smem.c:57-76), whose avail is itself computed from peer-writable SMEM words 'head = le32_to_cpu(*pipe->head); tail = le32_to_cpu(*pipe->tail);' (lines 70-71) pointing into the remote-partition SMEM item (qcom_smem_get at lines 60-68) - the bound is derived from the same attacker-controlled memory it is meant to validate, and chunk_size is never compared to pipe->native.length or any kernel-known maximum. Unsafe use: the intentless branch allocates 'intent->data = kmalloc(chunk_size + left_size, GFP_ATOMIC);' (line 813, unsigned int sum that can wrap) and 'intent->size = chunk_size + left_size;' (line 821), then the copy 'qcom_glink_rx_peak(glink, intent->data + intent->offset, sizeof(hdr), chunk_size);' (lines 850-851) and the advance 'ALIGN(sizeof(hdr) + chunk_size, 8)' (line 873) all trust the raw peer field; glink_smem_rx_peak copies count bytes with only a wraparound min() against native.length (qcom_glink_smem.c:82-97), so a peer-posted head beyond its fifo partition (or chunk_size beyond the real fifo length with a forged avail) drives an OOB read of shared memory into the kmalloc'ed intent buffer and later into the rpmsg callback. Counterevidence checked: the non-intentless branch's liid lookup drops unknown intents (lines 832-841); the 'intent->size - intent->offset < chunk_size' check (line 843) bounds the write into a previously negotiated intent but is itself computed from the kmalloc'ed peer sum at 813/821 for the intentless case; qcom_glink_handle_intent (lines 942+) uses struct_size + avail checks (the clamped sibling pattern) showing the same file does validate peer counts elsewhere. Attacker is the remote subsystem peer over SMEM; exploitation additionally requires the peer to post head/tail beyond its own fifo partition or a malicious modem-side firmware; no runtime reproducer was built.

candidates.reason: balloon_down(): peer-supplied req->range_count (raw __u32 of DM_UNBALLOON_REQUEST in static recv_buffer[PAGE_SIZE]) drives the free_balloon_pages() loop with no range check vs recvlen, PAGE_SIZE, or the guest's ballooned bookkeeping; dispatch path checks only recvlen > 0 (line 1495); reported as finding 1.

free_balloon_pages(): host-supplied 24-bit page_cnt and 40-bit start_frame (finfo fields, lines 1196-1197) drive pfn_to_page(i + start_frame) + __free_page() (lines 1202-1204) with no pfn_valid() and no cross-check against dm->num_pages_ballooned; num_pages_ballooned-- underflows; consuming use of finding 1.

Only validation of peer chunk_size is 'avail < sizeof(hdr) + chunk_size' where avail comes from glink_smem_rx_avail() reading peer-writable SMEM head/tail (qcom_glink_smem.c:70-76); kmalloc(chunk_size + left_size) at line 813 sizes a buffer from the same raw peer fields and the peak/copy at 850-851 advances by chunk_size; reported as finding 2.

head = le32_to_cpu(*pipe->head) / tail = le32_to_cpu(*pipe->tail) read from the remote-partition SMEM item acquired via qcom_smem_get (lines 60-68); the RX availability bound used to validate chunk_size is itself peer-controlled and never clamped to pipe->native.length; bound-source evidence for finding 2.

Sibling DM_MEM_HOT_ADD_REQUEST path validates the host header ('if (ha_msg->hdr.size == sizeof(struct dm_hot_add))'), the asymmetric-validation evidence that the same protocol enforces limits on one message type but not DM_UNBALLOON_REQUEST (1519-1523); this path itself is not the unclamped consumer.

hv_ringbuffer_read() sets *buffer_actual_len = packetlen from the ring descriptor and returns -ENOBUFS when packetlen > buflen, guaranteeing recvlen <= PAGE_SIZE and an exact-length memcpy into recv_buffer; the balloon OOB is driven by the peer range_count field, not by a mis-bounded receive.

DM_BALLOON_REQUEST path: host num_pages only bounds the guest allocation loop, which is itself bounded by the PAGE_SIZE bl_resp->hdr.size accumulation check (line 1223) and alloc_pages failure; the error unwind (1341-1345) frees only ranges the guest built in range_array; no peer count drives an unbounded kernel loop or allocation.
NTB peer-transport (ring/window based, peer-controlled MW/entries) was enumerated as present in s02 but not deep-read before the finalize directive; peer-field validation there is unverified.

9p virtio/socket transports (net/9p trans_virtio.c, trans_fd.c, trans_rdma.c, trans_xen.c and fs/9p consumers) present in s02 but only enumerated, not deep-read in this session; whether peer reply counts/lengths are cross-checked against client->msize locally is unverified here (prior rounds on other snapshots found them clamped).
NBD client reply handler present in s02 but not deep-read in this session; handle/tag cross-check and data-length handling unverified.

CIFS/ceph (fs/cifs, fs/ceph) server-reply parsers present in s02 but only enumerated, not deep-read in this session; server-supplied counts (e.g. DFS referral NumberOfReferrals) unverified in this tree.
virtio_rpmsg_bus.c and qcom_smd.c (alternate rpmsg framings of the same peer transport) present but not deep-read; peer message-length handling there is unverified.

limitations: The audit was bounded by the finalize directive: peer transports deep-read in s02 were drivers/hv/hv_balloon.c (+hv/ring_buffer.c receive semantics) and drivers/rpmsg/qcom_glink_native.c + qcom_glink_smem.c; ntb_transport, 9p trans_fd/virtio/rdma/xen, nbd, virtio_net receive_mergeable, vhost/vringh, cifs/ceph reply parsers, hv_kvp/hv_fcopy/hv_snapshot utils channels, xen pvcalls/xenbus, and network admin-queue reply handlers were enumerated by directory/grep listing only and remain unverified (recorded as unresolved candidates).

Both findings are source-level invariant violations, not proven exploits: the hv_balloon attacker is the Hyper-V host peer (semi-trusted hypervisor in the drivers/hv threat model, weaker than a remote network attacker), and impact of range_count > ~PAGE_SIZE/16 is an OOB read of static .bss beyond recv_buffer plus pfn_to_page()/__free_page() on host-chosen PFNs without pfn_valid() - corruption/crash is argued from source, not demonstrated at runtime.

The glink finding requires the remote subsystem peer to post head (or chunk_size) beyond its own fifo partition / forge avail in shared SMEM, or unsigned wrap in kmalloc(chunk_size + left_size); which glink transport instances (smem vs rpm) are actually bound in s02's build configs was not verified, and no path delivering the copied bytes to userspace was traced.

greybus (the f002/f013 beagleplay/es2 analogue) does not exist in s02 (drivers/greybus absent), so that variant family is not applicable to this snapshot; the seed usbip code is excluded by rule and was not examined.

No compilation, static-analyzer run, or runtime reproducer was performed (assigned tree is read-only); all line numbers come from direct sed/grep reads in this session, with the balloon_down/free_balloon_pages/callback windows and the glink rx_data/smem_avail windows re-verified line-by-line before reporting.
